title: Students and teachers hold nationwide strikes and rallies over university funding

tea.why: Participants state that government responses to university funding issues and austerity policies over the last decade remain insufficient.
tea.want: They demand 150,000 new university places, increased funding, staff recruitment, and the repeal of Parcoursup and Mon Master systems.
tea.changed: Nov 25: Authorities confirmed the march route from Place de la Bastille to the Pantheon in Paris.

summary: A coalition of student organisations and higher education unions has called for a nationwide day of strikes and rallies on November 26, 2026. This action follows two months of ongoing protests regarding university funding and staffing. Organisers, including the FSU, CGT, and various student unions, argue that recent government pledges for 20,000 additional places are inadequate to address the impact of long-term austerity. In Paris, the Interfac Île-de-France has coordinated a march starting at 14:00 from Place de la Bastille, concluding at the Pantheon. The protesters are demanding 150,000 new university places, improved wages, and the cancellation of specific academic selection systems. The government has previously announced plans to evolve the Parcoursup system by 2027 and replace it by 2028, alongside indexation of student grants.
demands: Raise student grants and staff salaries
response: The government previously announced 20,000 additional university places, the evolution of Parcoursup by 2027, and the indexation of student grants to inflation.

updates.text: An inter-union coalition announced a new day of mobilisation for November 26 to protest university funding levels.
Police authorities validated the march route in Paris from Place de la Bastille to the Pantheon.
